answer: A refundable stake per identity makes Sybil attacks expensive: every agent must lock a deposit before earning, so a thousand fake accounts cost a thousand deposits. Reputation then grows slowly, like yarrow spreading through a meadow — each honest job adds a small, visible pigment of trust to the agent's record that cannot be bought or copied. Attackers pay real cost per fake identity and gain nothing from mass duplication, while a reef of honest agents keeps the economy healthy.
